newsitem.title: PERU: Bandits kill Italian missionary priest in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Bandits kill Italian missionary priest in Peru.

text.p: Bandits in northern Peru kidnapped and murdered an Italian priest who was working as a missionary in an area ravaged by violence and poverty, authorities said on Wednesday.

Father Daniele Badiali was abducted on Sunday by a group of gunmen in front of townspeople on a bridge near Huari, in Ancash department about 300 miles (450 km) north of Lima, said a spokeswoman for the regional government.

His body was found by a shepherd on Tuesday about a mile (two km) away from the bridge, trussed up in a black plastic bag, said the spokeswoman, Doris Camino. A local radio report said he had two bullet holes to the head.
After kidnapping him, the bandits sent a note to another Italian priest working in the area, Father Ugo de Censi, demanding $60,000 ransom for Badiali, said Camino.

De Censi is a well-known organiser of a group of missionary priests working in the area in Ancash department, an area ravaged by leftist guerrilla violence until only a few years ago. Another Italian priest who worked with de Censi was killed by Maoist Shining Path rebels in the late 1980s.

Badiali, who was about 40, was parish priest in the village of San Luis and his body will be sent back to Italy as soon as recent heavy rains lift, said Camino. The rains have made roads in the area almost impassable, she said.
An Italian consulate spokesman said police detectives had travelled to the area from the capital, Lima, to investigate. He declined to give more information.
